<reason>A more convincingly distinguished privacy protection from accessibility, and blocked visits from reduced harmful exposure. It directly answered the gambling comparison through transaction-level control and clarified that its alternative involved mandatory safer defaults, not today's checkbox. B supplied a plausible friction mechanism and useful fallback proposals, but repeatedly overstated their effectiveness and mischaracterized A's concessions. Its complaint about unanswered pressure also preceded A's scheduled response. A did not prove displacement would erase all benefits, but successfully showed why B's claimed benefits and minimized burdens did not establish the combined mandate's proportionality.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A undercut B's alcohol analogy by contrasting restricted physical supply with following another link. Under pressure, B repeated where exposure supposedly begins rather than explaining why gating that starting point would eliminate most exposure. A explicitly accepted some benefit while exposing that unsupported extrapolation.</best_rebuttal>
